subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but the correct solution depends on durable storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, and migration choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Narrow to memory-core v1
options.body: Limit the first implementation to bundled memory-core CLI and SQLite behavior, accepting a later alignment step for external memory plugins.

options.title: Defer lifecycle MVP
options.body: Leave current search, promotion, and dreaming behavior in place while tracking concrete stale-memory bugs separately until lifecycle work becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory docs and memory-tool integration history make this the best available routing candidate for cross-plugin lifecycle product direction.
